- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially in the first 5–10 days after the forecast window starts.
- Model tends to overestimate prices after sharp spikes in the history (e.g., after 90.01 or 86.03), often overshooting by 2–5% and then correcting.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing the true mean reversion trend — it delays the downward correction after peaks.
- Model exhibits a strong bias toward lower values in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 15–25), often missing the true peak or trough.
- Model frequently fails to adjust for the “recovery” phase after a sharp drop — it underreacts to low prices and doesn’t anticipate rebound.
- Model tends to overfit to recent high values, especially if the last 5–7 days are high, leading to overestimation of future prices.
- Model underestimates the true volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window, often missing the downward correction or sudden drop.
- Model shows a tendency to “smooth” out sharp transitions — it avoids sudden jumps or drops in the forecast, leading to lagged or muted responses.
